expected_value_creation: Turn repeated, adjudicated ambiguity into an explicit candidate rubric change whose source, wording, alternatives, impact, authorization, replay requirement, implementation, and rollback remain auditable.
beneficiary: QIF users and affected stakeholders who need evaluator criteria to improve without hidden mutation or false consensus
supporting_evidence: OpenAI describes grader prompts as iterative and recommends adding discovered edge cases to grader evals.
NIST ARIA and TEVV guidance require customized evaluation using model, red-team, and user evidence rather than one static rubric.
Recent research shows expert rubrics can suppress visible disagreement without resolving interpretation and that judge behavior can depend on rubric wording and downstream consequence.
success_criteria: Every revision candidate links to adjudicated disagreement and exact affected rubric clauses.
Rejected and deferred alternatives, dissent, reviewers, and authority remain preserved.
Implemented revisions require approval, replay scope, evidence, and rollback plan; no automatic mutation is allowed.
The verifier reproduces lifecycle, references, counts, state transitions, and governance without claiming semantic improvement.
